analysis:
Reviewed the sandbox docs and the eligibility code. No regression was found in the visible lines.

Eligibility code (provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/Sandbox/SandboxEligibility.swift):
- diskShortfall (head 225-227) now adds linux.plannedBytes and macOS.plannedBytes plus platform.nextSlotBytes.
- plannedBytes is defined at head 309.
- freeSpaceNote (head 271-278) is a new advisory string built from plan fields. It interpolates only the integer gibUp(short) (head 277).
- These are display-only sizing changes. They have no trust, auth, crypto or IPC effect.
- The plan values come from the add-on installer (TB-013). The add-on already runs as the owner, so a misleading figure grants nothing new.

Docs:
- docs/provider/sandboxes.md head 85-95 describes a new behavior: on an already-set-up Mac, setup asks the installer for its plan again and offers the new slot counts.
- With --yes or without a terminal, setup applies them only when slots are added and none removed.
- head 120-125 says the installer refuses rather than waits while a job runs, and that setup never passes --force.
- docs/provider/cli-reference.md unit 15 (head 2380-2553) is unchanged context.

SandboxSetupCommand.swift (unit 4ef4ced1e3c7d2e1:0):
- Only metadata was supplied; no source or patch text is visible.
- The file_changes excerpt shows .alreadySetUp now calls reportAndRecheckSizing(status). Before, it printed status and changed nothing.
- install() now receives options. Head 151-228 is new code.

Integration must verify the following, because rerunning setup on a configured Mac now downloads and executes install.sh as the owner (TB-013, T-061, A-019) where the base did not:
- the same HTTPS/verification path is used for the recheck;
- the installer's plan output is parsed with bounds and strict types;
- the non-interactive auto-apply cannot remove slots or pass --force;
- it is skipped while jobs run, per the docs.
- Check the A-018 availability effect: the add-on restarts and the hold (TB-012) is handled when slots are reinstalled.

This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a problem.
